newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela public sector surplus seen 7.3 pct GDP.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela public sector surplus seen 7.3 pct GDP.

text.p: Venezuela is expected to register a 1996 consolidated public sector budget surplus equivalent to 7.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) exceeding the IMF's 1.2 percent target, the Central Bank said in its annual year end review of the Venezuelan economy.

With fiscal accounts boosted by high international oil prices, the central government's budget is also expected to close the year with a 0.9 percent GDP surplus, compared with IMF targets of 3.3 percent and last year's 4.8 percent deficit, the Central Bank document said.

"This favorable result is primarily due to the rise in fiscal revenues, that grew 169.6 percent in nominal terms...In terms of GDP total revenues increased from 15.9 percent in 1995 to 22.00 percent in 1996," the Central Bank said.
The rise in revenues was attributed to high oil prices, the devaluation of the bolivar in mid-April and the payment of dividends by state-owned oil company PdVSA.
Government spending rose in real terms from 20.8 percent of GDP in 1995 to 21.0 percent, the Bank added.
